verdict_text:
YES

The regex matches exactly the seven per-layer projection names (112 tensors) via `fullmatch`, casts them with `.to(torch.bfloat16)` (round-to-nearest-even) from float32, leaves every other tensor as float32 with unchanged values, changes no names, and deletes nothing — `buffer_re` contains `(?!)`, a lookahead that can never succeed, so the `continue` branch is dead code, which is harmless here since the checkpoint has no buffers. All four required checks are asserted before the write, and the sharded write is delegated to `save_sharded_safetensors` with the specified 268,435,456-byte limit and output directory. The only part I cannot verify from this file alone is the helper's shard-packing and index-emission behavior in `_ckpt`, which is not part of the artifact shown.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
